radiology_report:
Antoni van Leeuwenhoek
Department of Radiology
Date: 12 Dec 2024
Exam: mpMRI Prostate
Clinical indication: PSA 17.0 ng/mL, prior negative biopsy, elevated PSA density.
FINDINGS: Prostate volume measures 48.89 mL. T2-weighted imaging demonstrates a well-defined, hypointense lesion in the peripheral zone of the left posterior mid-gland, measuring approximately 18 x 14 x 16 mm. The lesion shows marked restricted diffusion on DWI (b=1400) with corresponding low ADC values. Dynamic contrast-enhanced sequences reveal early, intense enhancement of the lesion. No extracapsular extension or seminal vesicle invasion is identified.
IMPRESSION: PI-RADS 5 lesion in the left posterior peripheral zone. Prostate volume 48.89 mL, PSA density 0.35 ng/mL/mL. Clinical stage cT1c. csPCa predicted probability 0.86317605.

previous_notes.author: Dr. N. Kuiper (GP)
previous_notes.text: Patient attended for routine follow-up. PSA was measured at 9.5 ng/mL, showing a significant rise from the previous value of 5.3 ng/mL in July 2023. Given the persistent elevation and rising trend, a repeat multiparametric MRI was arranged to evaluate for any new suspicious lesions prior to considering further tissue sampling.

previous_notes.author: Dr. N. Kuiper (GP)
previous_notes.text: Follow-up consultation regarding the markedly elevated PSA of 17.0 ng/mL. The patient reported mild lower urinary tract symptoms but denied any bone pain or systemic symptoms. A recent mpMRI at Antoni van Leeuwenhoek revealed a PI-RADS 5 lesion. The patient is referred for urological re-evaluation to discuss the discrepancy between the imaging findings and the prior negative biopsy results.
